cues.zh: 好吧，冬季供暖季马上就要到了
cues.en: Welp, winter heating season is quickly approaching

cues.zh: （至少在北半球是这样）
cues.en: (in the northern hemisphere anyway)

cues.zh: 这意味着我们很多人几个月来第一次打开供暖系统，并祈祷它别出幺蛾子。
cues.en: which means that many of us are firing up our heating systems for the first time in many months and hoping for the best.

cues.zh: 你有没有想过，为什么你家的暖气炉会发出那些奇奇怪怪的声音？
cues.en: Have you ever wondered why your furnace makes the noises that it does?

cues.zh: 还有，它为什么看起来是一步一步按阶段运行的？
cues.en: And how come it seems to work in distinct steps?

cues.zh: 热交换器到底是什么？
cues.en: What’s a heat exchanger?

cues.zh: 为什么我们需要担心一氧化碳中毒？
cues.en: Why do I need to be worried about carbon monoxide poisoning?

cues.zh: 我们到底为什么要用暖气炉？
cues.en: Why do we use furnaces at all?

cues.zh: 问得好！正因如此，我专门做了个视频来解答这些问题。
cues.en: Great questions! So great that I’m making a video to answer them.

cues.zh: 首先，本期视频要讲的是典型的北美强制风冷式燃气
cues.en: Now first, we’re gonna be talking about the typical forced-air gas-fired North American

cues.zh: 供暖系统，因为我住的地方普遍用这个，我也最容易接触到。
cues.en: heating system in this video because that’s what’s common where I live and what I have access to.

cues.zh: 在过去半个世纪左右建造的、地处寒冷气候的中小型建筑中，
cues.en: Pretty much every small to medium-sized building over here constructed in the last

cues.zh: 几乎每一栋都至少装有一台这样的设备来提供暖气。
cues.en: half century or so in a winter climate has at least one of these providing it with heat.

cues.zh: 如果你习惯了由中央锅炉和暖气片组成的供暖系统，那眼前的这个可不是。
cues.en: If you’re used to a heating system with a central boiler and radiators, well this ain’t that.

cues.zh: 这种系统在北美并不罕见，但通常仅限于那些老建筑，
cues.en: Those aren’t exactly rare in North America, but are typically limited to older buildings that were constructed

cues.zh: 建造于我们对空调上瘾之前。
cues.en: before we became addicted to air conditioning.

cues.zh: 自中央空调普及以来，我们就定型成了这种风道系统，
cues.en: Ever since central air conditioning became common, we’ve settled on ducted systems like this

cues.zh: 暖风机既是冬季的供暖热源，又是夏季空调的
cues.en: where a furnace acts as both the heat source for winter months and air handler for the air conditioner

cues.zh: 空气处理单元。
cues.en: in the summer months.

cues.zh: 我们先来了解一下暖风机最基本的作用是什么。
cues.en: Let’s start by asking what the basic job of the furnace is.

cues.zh: 你可能会说，那显然是给生活空间供暖啊——
cues.en: You might say, well obviously it’s to provide heat for a living space -

cues.zh: 你基本算说对了！
cues.en: and you’d be more-or-less right!

cues.zh: 但更具体地说，它的作用是尽可能安全地释放可燃燃料中所含的热能，
cues.en: But more specifically, its job is to safely release as much of the heat energy contained in a combustible fuel that it can

cues.zh: 输送到居住空间，并通过鼓风机和风道网络将其分发出去。
cues.en: into the living space and distribute it with the aid of a blower fan and ductwork.

cues.zh: 锅炉里几乎所有设计都围绕安全展开，
cues.en: Nearly everything in the furnace is designed around safety,

cues.zh: 它的操作序列专门用于验证各部件的完整性和功能，
cues.en: and its sequence of operations is performed specifically to prove the integrity and functionality

cues.zh: 确认无误后才允许自身运行。
cues.en: of each of its components before it allows itself to run.

cues.zh: 如果自检失败，它就会锁定自己，你就得叫当地的暖通公司了。
cues.en: If it fails its own tests, it locks itself out and you’ll need to call your local HVAC company.

cues.zh: 总比丢了命强！
cues.en: Better that than be dead!

cues.zh: 我们稍后会详细讲这套操作序列以及各个部件，但首先，
cues.en: We’ll go over that sequence of operations as well as the components themselves shortly but first,

cues.zh: 先说说我们为什么要用这些东西。
cues.en: let’s discuss why we use these things.

cues.zh: 对于不在北美生活的人来说，这类设备似乎总让人摸不着头脑。
cues.en: These seem to invite a sort of bafflement in those who don’t live in North America.

cues.zh: 如果你习惯的是锅炉，那倒说得通，但我经常遇到一些人，似乎认为
cues.en: If a boiler is what you’re used to, well that makes sense, but quite often I’ve run across folks who seem to think

cues.zh: 我们的暖炉在某种程度上是低效的机器。
cues.en: our furnaces are somehow inefficient machines.

cues.zh: 完全不是，这些非常高效。
cues.en: Not at all, these are incredibly efficient.

cues.zh: 这台特定的炉子能捕获燃料中96%的热能。
cues.en: This particular furnace is able to capture 96% of the heat energy in a fuel.

cues.zh: 那很棒，但有些型号能得到更多！
cues.en: That’s excellent, but some models get even more than that!

cues.zh: 嗨，我是来自未来的我，带着一个尴尬的更正。
cues.en: Hi, it’s me from the future with an embarrassing correction.

cues.zh: 所以我们要谈论的是AFUE，也就是“A-few”，代表年度燃料利用效率。
cues.en: So we’re about to talk about the AFUE or “A-few” which stands for annual fuel utilization efficiency.

cues.zh: 对于这台炉子来说，它是95。
cues.en: And for this furnace It’s 95.

cues.zh: 不是96。在此之前，我有无数机会查看这个标签，
cues.en: Not 96. I had countless opportunities to look at this label before now,

cues.zh: 可惜我一个都没看。
cues.en: alas I took none of them.

cues.zh: 我的记忆辜负了我。
cues.en: And my memory failed me.

cues.zh: 所以在接下来的视频中，如果我说“96”
cues.en: So for the rest of this video, if I say “96”

cues.zh: 我可能指的是95。
cues.en: I probably meant 95.

cues.zh: 不管怎样，回到AFUE。
cues.en: Anyway, back to the AFUE.

cues.zh: 它是按差不多年度平均值来测量的，以帮助解释效率上的差异
cues.en: It’s measured as a more-or-less yearly average to help account for the differences in efficiency

cues.zh: 在启动和关闭时。在稳定加热状态下，它实际上稍高一些。
cues.en: at start-up and shut-down. During a steady heating state it’s actually slightly higher.

cues.zh: 能把燃料中96%的可用热能送入室内，这非常了不起，
cues.en: Being able to get 96% of the heat energy available in a fuel into the living space is tremendous,

cues.zh: 但即便是市面上最差的天然气炉，AFUE也至少有80。
cues.en: but even the worst natural gas furnaces on the market have at least an AFUE of 80.

cues.zh: 很久以前我做过一个视频，专门讲燃烧燃料供暖背后的道理，
cues.en: A long time ago I made a video specifically about the rationale behind burning fuel for space heating,

cues.zh: 但基本上就是这个原因。
cues.en: but this is essentially it.

cues.zh: 炉子在燃烧燃料、尽可能提取其中能量方面非常出色。
cues.en: Furnaces excel at burning fuel and capturing nearly everything we can from it.

cues.zh: 话虽如此，随着我们走向电气化，它们大概（也希望如此）正在被淘汰。
cues.en: That said, they’re probably (and, hopefully) on their way out as we move towards electrification.

cues.zh: 不过，我们通常不会用电阻加热来给整个住宅供暖，因为
cues.en: Now, we don’t typically use electric resistive heating to heat entire homes because,

cues.zh: 虽然电加热本身是100%高效的，但发电并不是。
cues.en: while electric heat is itself 100% efficient, electrical generation is not.

cues.zh: 即便发电是100%高效，电阻加热的用电需求在大规模上也不切实际。
cues.en: And even if it were, the electrical requirements of resistive heat aren’t practical on a large scale.

cues.zh: 但热泵能彻底颠覆这个算法。
cues.en: But heat pumps are able to turn this math on its head.

cues.zh: 因为热泵本质上就是反向运行的空调，它能搬运的能量远大于自身消耗的能量，
cues.en: Since heat pumps, which are basically just air conditioners running in reverse, can move much more energy than they themselves consume,

cues.zh: 所以它无疑是家庭供暖的未来。
cues.en: they’re undoubtedly the future of home space heating.

cues.zh: 即便在目前以化石燃料为主的电网下，它产生的碳排放也比直接燃烧燃料更少，
cues.en: Even right now with our majority fossil-grid, they result in fewer carbon emissions than directly burning fuel

cues.zh: 因为它的效率可以接近500%——
cues.en: because they’re efficiency can approach 500% -

cues.zh: 足以抵消发电环节的损耗。
cues.en: more than accounting for the losses in generation.

cues.zh: 不过这个话题（以及它当前的挑战）我们留到未来一个视频再讲，我保证不会太久。
cues.en: But we’ll save that topic (and its current challenges) for a video in the I Promise not-too-distant future.

cues.zh: 但现在，还是回到这个吧！
cues.en: For now, though, back to this!

cues.zh: 这些年来，在投身这项人类事业的过程中，我们学到的一件事就是：燃烧东西并不好受。
cues.en: One of the things we’ve learned over the years as we’ve embarked on this human endeavor is that burning things is unpleasant.

cues.zh: 燃烧几乎任何燃料，包括所谓的“清洁燃烧”天然气
cues.en: Burning pretty much any fuel, including the so-called “clean burning” natural gas

cues.zh: 都会产生颗粒物，吸入对身体不好，当然还有更
cues.en: produces particulate matter which isn’t great to breathe, and of course there’s the much more

cues.zh: 直接致命的燃烧副产物一氧化碳，由于进化上的不幸，
cues.en: immediately deadly combustion by-product carbon monoxide which, through evolutionary bad luck,

cues.zh: 它比氧气更容易吸引你的红细胞。
cues.en: is much more appealing to your red blood cells than oxygen.

cues.zh: 这可不妙。
cues.en: Which is bad.

cues.zh: 所以一般来说，我们不该在室内燃烧东西。
cues.en: So generally, we shouldn’t burn things indoors.

cues.zh: 然而，这里有个设备却在室内燃烧东西……
cues.en: And yet, here’s a device which burns things… indoors.

cues.zh: 啊！但这台特定的炉子是一台冷凝炉，
cues.en: Ah! But this particular furnace is a condensing furnace,

cues.zh: 多亏了这里的两根管道，燃料的燃烧某种程度上发生在室外——不过这个稍后再讲。
cues.en: and thanks to these two pipes here, the combustion of the fuel sort of happens outside - but more on that later.

cues.zh: 你可能还知道另一种在室内不通风燃烧燃料的设备——常见的灶台和烤箱，
cues.en: You may also know of a certain other device which does burn fuel indoors without ventilation - the common stovetop and oven,

cues.zh: 研究开始表明，这或许也不太好，但有一点小小的安慰
cues.en: and research is beginning to suggest that maybe this isn’t so great either, but there is the small saving grace

cues.zh: 烹饪燃烧的燃料量通常只是炉子所用的一小部分，
cues.en: that the quantities of fuel burned for cooking are generally small fractions of that which a furnace uses,

cues.zh: 而且也有办法通过通风来缓解，不过这就扯远了。
cues.en: and also there are ways to mitigate this through ventilation but I digress.

cues.zh: 像这样的炉子需要燃烧燃料供暖，接下来还得费力排出废气。
cues.en: Anyway, a furnace like this needs to burn its heating fuel and then it has a bit of an exhausting job ahead of itself.

cues.zh: 费力排气。
cues.en: Exhausting.

cues.zh: 我们要让燃烧产生的副产物排到室外
cues.en: We want the byproducts of the combustion process to make their way outside

cues.zh: 这样它们就只会在大约……十年或二十年后才造成问题。
cues.en: where they’ll only be problematic in about… a decade or two.

cues.zh: 当然，我们还要把燃烧产生的热量提取出来，送进生活空间。
cues.en: But of course we want to be able to extract the heat generated by the combustion process and release that into the living space.

cues.zh: 这可以通过热交换器来实现。
cues.en: We can do that with a heat exchanger.

cues.zh: 在典型的炉子里，热交换器由一系列管子组成。
cues.en: In a typical furnace, this takes the form of a series of tubes.

cues.zh: 不过，实际上！
cues.en: Actually, though!

cues.zh: 标准的 80+ 炉子里，热交换器其实就是若干根通常呈 U 形的钢管。
cues.en: The heat exchanger in a standard 80+ furnace is simply some number of typically U-shaped steel tubes.

cues.zh: 你可以叫它们 U 形管。
cues.en: You might call them U-tubes.

cues.zh: 燃料在这些管子里燃烧，当然会让管子变得烫得要命。
cues.en: The fuel is burned inside these tubes, which of course makes them get pretty freaking hot.

cues.zh: 然后，这些管子会被置于鼓风电机吹过炉膛的气流通道中，
cues.en: Those tubes, then, are put in the path of air being forced through the furnace with the aid of a blower motor,

cues.zh: 这股气流通过给管道降温，防止热交换器熔化，
cues.en: and that air keeps the heat exchanger from melting by cooling the tubes down,

cues.zh: 顺便也就把空气给加热了。这算是个不错的好处。
cues.en: which also incidentally heats the air. That’s a nice bonus.

cues.zh: 这样做的实际效果就是，燃料产生的热量被释放到流经炉膛的空气中，
cues.en: The practical upshot of this is that the heat from the fuel gets released into the air flowing through the furnace

cues.zh: 最终从通风口排出为全屋供暖，但燃烧副产物仍被隔绝在那些管道内。
cues.en: and eventually out of the vents which heat your home, but the combustion byproducts stay separated inside those tubes.

cues.zh: 当然，我们得想办法把这些副产物排出去。
cues.en: And of course, we need those by-products to go away somehow.

cues.zh: 而且等等，燃烧燃料需要氧气，而燃烧过程会消耗氧气——
cues.en: And also, hang on, you need oxygen to burn fuels and the burning of the fuel consumes that oxygen -

cues.zh: 所以除了排出副产物之外，你还需要一种方法给这些管道通入新鲜空气。
cues.en: so you’re gonna need a way to supply those tubes with fresh air in addition to getting rid of the byproducts.

cues.zh: 哈！现在我们要聊到炉子更实用也更关乎安全的部分了。
cues.en: Aha! Well now we’re getting into the more practical and safety bits of the furnace.

cues.zh: 如果你用过这种炉子，大概会注意到有两个鼓风机电机。
cues.en: If you’ve ever lived with a furnace like this, you’ll likely have noticed that there are two blower motors.

cues.zh: 大的那个负责把空气从出风口送出来。
cues.en: There’s the big one that makes air come out of your registers.

cues.zh: 但在它启动之前，你会听到另一个的声音。
cues.en: But before that one comes on, you hear another one.

cues.zh: 那是干什么用的？
cues.en: What’s that for?

cues.zh: 可以说，它才是炉子最重要的部分。
cues.en: Well, that’s arguably the most important part of the furnace.

cues.zh: 这个鼓风机叫引风电机，其实它更像是个抽风机。
cues.en: This blower is called the draft inducer, and really it’s more of a sucker.

cues.zh: 它把空气——以及后来的其他有趣气体——抽过热交换器。
cues.en: It pulls air - and later, other fun gasses - through the heat exchanger.

cues.zh: 换句话说，它制造了一股气流。
cues.en: In other words, it induces a draft.

cues.zh: 然后这些空气被推上去，穿过某种烟囱，最终排出屋外，
cues.en: That air then gets pushed up through some sort of chimney where it will eventually exit the home,

cues.zh: 或者像这里这样，通过这根PVC管排出。
cues.en: or as is the case here it exits through this PVC pipe.

cues.zh: 引风机位于热交换器的排气侧，因此会把空气吸过管道，
cues.en: The draft inducer lives on the exit side of the heat exchanger, so it pulls air through the tubes,

cues.zh: 而管道另一侧装着喷火器。
cues.en: and what lives on the other side of those tubes are the flamethrowers.

cues.zh: 现在说到燃烧这部分了。
cues.en: Now we’re getting to the burny business.

cues.zh: 燃料要燃烧，就得先有燃料，
cues.en: If we’re burning a fuel, it’s gotta come from somewhere,

cues.zh: 而燃料来自地下深处，在那里被封存了数千年，直到我们把它开采出来。
cues.en: and where it comes from is deep underground having been trapped there for millennia before we extracted it.

cues.zh: 不过对你的暖炉来说，燃料是从燃烧器里出来的。
cues.en: But as far as your furnace is concerned it comes from the burners.

cues.zh: 燃烧器本质上就是专用喷嘴，会向热交换器的管道中喷出一定量的燃气。
cues.en: These are essentially just specialized nozzles which release some amount of gas into the heat exchanger’s tubes.

cues.zh: 有了引风机持续送入新鲜空气，
cues.en: Thanks to the constant supply of fresh air brought about by the draft inducer,

cues.zh: 燃气就能充分燃烧。
cues.en: it will burn quite nicely.

cues.zh: 引风机不仅能确保燃烧时有新鲜空气，
cues.en: The draft inducer ensures not only that there is fresh air for burning

cues.zh: 还会防止热交换器管道另一端排出的气体进入居住空间，
cues.en: but also that what comes out the other side of the heat exchanger tubes doesn’t make it into the living space

cues.zh: 而是将它们安全地排到室外。
cues.en: and is instead safely expelled outdoors.

cues.zh: 因为这个设备要处理可燃燃料和密闭空间的危险组合，
cues.en: Because this device deals with the, frankly, dangerous combination of combustible fuels and enclosed spaces,

cues.zh: 所以它设计了多重安全联锁和一系列操作流程，确保不会出大问题。
cues.en: it’s designed with a number of safety interlocks and a sequence of operations to ensure things don’t go too terribly wrong.

cues.zh: 但在我们深入之前，
cues.en: But before we get into that,

cues.zh: 我知道这是第二句"但在我们深入之前"，
cues.en: I know this is the second "but before we get into that,"

cues.zh: 抱歉，
cues.en: apologies,

cues.zh: 我们先聊聊这个炉子的冷凝部分。
cues.en: let’s discuss the condensing part of this furnace.

cues.zh: 当你燃烧天然气这类燃料时，副产物之一就是水蒸气。
cues.en: When you burn a fuel like natural gas, one of the byproducts is water vapor.

cues.zh: 标准的80+炉子不太知道该怎么处理它，所以就直接把它和一氧化碳以及其他脏东西一起排出去了。
cues.en: A standard 80+ furnace doesn't really know what to make of that so sends it out with the carbon monoxide and other icky stuff.

cues.zh: 但那些水蒸气是热的，更重要的是它以潜热的形式储存着能量。
cues.en: But that water vapor is hot, and more importantly holds energy in the form of latent heat.

cues.zh: 当它凝结成液体时——这是必然会发生的——
cues.en: When it condenses into a liquid, as it will inevitably do -

cues.zh: 也就是寒冬腊月里你看到从屋顶冒出来的那些蒸汽——
cues.en: that’s all the steam you see coming from the rooftops of homes in the dead of winter -

cues.zh: 它就会释放出那份能量。
cues.en: it releases that energy.

cues.zh: 但如果这一切只是发生在外面，那就没用了。
cues.en: But that’s no good if it’s just happening outside.

cues.zh: 如果我们能让它在内部冷凝，就能从加热燃料中获得更多能量。
cues.en: If we could make it condense inside, we’d be able to get more energy out of the heating fuel.

cues.zh: 所以，冷凝式炉在主火管之后基本上还有一个二次换热器
cues.en: And so, a condensing furnace has what is essentially a second heat exchanger after the main fire tubes

cues.zh: 它的表面积更大，能进一步冷却废气
cues.en: with a greater surface area that can cool the exhaust gases further

cues.zh: 这本身就有助于从燃料中获取更多热量，但更重要的是，它能让大部分水蒸气
cues.en: which helps get more heat out of the fuel all by itself, but more importantly it gets most of the water vapor

cues.zh: 在炉内冷凝并释放潜热，而不是排到室外空气中被浪费掉。
cues.en: to condense and release its latent heat inside the furnace rather than to outside air where it is otherwise wasted.

cues.zh: 这就是这种炉子能把燃料中96%的可用能量送入家中的原因。
cues.en: That’s how this furnace is able to get 96% of the energy available in the fuel into the home.

cues.zh: 这也是它能通过PVC管排气的原因。
cues.en: And it’s also how it’s able to exhaust through a PVC pipe.

cues.zh: 想想看，它在燃烧可燃气体，里面真的有火，
cues.en: I mean, think about this, it’s burning flammable gas, there’s literal fire inside of it,

cues.zh: 却能输出70,000 BTU，约20千瓦的热量。
cues.en: and it outputs 70,000 BTUS or about 20 kilowatts of heat.

cues.zh: 然而，它在废气中损失的热量很少，因此可以安全地通过几乎不发热的塑料管排出。
cues.en: And yet, it loses so little of that heat in the exhaust that it can safely exit through a plastic pipe which barely gets warm at all.

cues.zh: 相比之下，80+ 炉子配有钢制排烟管，热得你甚至不能碰，
cues.en: Compare that to an 80+ furnace with a steel exhaust chimney that gets so hot you can’t even touch it,

cues.zh: 你就会明白为什么冷凝炉如此重要，是个绝佳的主意。
cues.en: and you’ll understand why condensing furnaces are a big deal and a great idea.

cues.zh: 当然，冷凝炉比传统炉子要复杂一些。
cues.en: A condensing furnace is a little more complicated, of course, than a conventional one.

cues.zh: 这主要因为处理冷凝水并不是件容易的事
cues.en: Most of that has to do with the fact that dealing with the condensate isn’t the easiest task

cues.zh: 首先，以前不用管，现在你得处理它了。
cues.en: for one, well now you have to deal with it when previously you didn’t.

cues.zh: 这台炉子侧面有个排水管，正是为此设计的。
cues.en: This furnace has a drain pipe on its side for that very reason.

cues.zh: 而且那水不是普通水，由于其他燃烧副产物，它酸性相当强
cues.en: But also that water isn’t just plain water, it’s pretty acidic thanks to other combustion byproducts

cues.zh: 所以二级热交换器需要用不锈钢等耐腐蚀材料制造。
cues.en: so the secondary heat exchanger needs to be made of materials, such as stainless steel, which resist corrosion.

cues.zh: 这多少会增加炉子的成本，但在我看来，能从取暖燃料中多榨出10%到15%的能量，
cues.en: This adds somewhat to the cost of the furnace, but getting an extra 10 or 15% of the energy out of your heating fuel makes it, to my mind,

cues.zh: 显然是值得的，我们绝对应该想办法补贴这部分额外成本，
cues.en: obviously worth it and we absolutely should find ways to help subsidize the added cost

cues.zh: 帮助那些需要经济援助的人，因为长远来看，这总能节省金钱和资源。
cues.en: for those who need financial assistance because in the long run it will always save money and resources.

cues.zh: 坦白说，到这一步就是显而易见的选择。
cues.en: It’s frankly a no-brainer at this point.

cues.zh: 哦，还有那根管子？这是另一种提高效率的办法。
cues.en: Oh, and that other pipe there? Well, here’s another way to get an increase in efficiency.

cues.zh: 这个炉子从室外获取氧气供应。
cues.en: This furnace gets its oxygen supply from outside.

cues.zh: 这根管子只是为燃烧部分提供室外空气，
cues.en: This pipe is simply supplying the combustion section with outside air,

cues.zh: 实际上你可以看到它只是通向这个空间（另一端在室外）。
cues.en: in fact you can see that it just opens to this space (and the other end is outside).

cues.zh: 为什么要这样做？
cues.en: Why do that?

cues.zh: 因为传统炉子是从它所在的房间获取燃烧空气的。
cues.en: Well, a conventional furnace gets its combustion air from the room it’s sitting in.

cues.zh: 也就是说，只要引风机在运行，就会产生负压，
cues.en: That means it creates negative pressure whenever the draft inducer is running,

cues.zh: 从而引入一些室外冷空气，来补充从排气管排出的空气。
cues.en: and that brings in some amount of cold outside air to replace what leaves through the exhaust.

cues.zh: 相比之下，这根进气管，加上这块面板上的密封，使得炉子的燃烧部分
cues.en: In contrast, this supply pipe, along with the seals in this panel, makes it so that the combustion section of the furnace

cues.zh: 基本上完全处于室外，完全不产生负压。
cues.en: is essentially entirely outdoors, creating no negative pressure at all.

cues.zh: 当然，尤其是在当下的人类经验中，我们正发现
cues.en: Of course, particularly right now in the human experience we’re discovering

cues.zh: 我们其实应该比现在有更多的空气交换。
cues.en: that we really ought to have a little more exchange of air than we do.

cues.zh: 我们大多数效率优先的建筑做法，都源于七十年代的能源危机，
cues.en: Most of our efficiency-first building practices came about thanks to the energy crises of the seventies,

cues.zh: 而我们一直住在基本密封的盒子里，结果发现这并不太好，
cues.en: and we’ve been living in mostly sealed boxes which it turns out isn’t super great,

cues.zh: 而且不仅仅是因为呼吸道传染病大流行。
cues.en: and not just because of respiratory disease pandemics.

cues.zh: 呼出的二氧化碳单纯积聚起来就很危险，所以保持一定程度的负压可能是件好事，
cues.en: Simple build-up of carbon dioxide from our exhalation can be hazardous, so some amount of negative pressure is probably a good thing

cues.zh: 这个话题也值得更多关注和研究。
cues.en: and this topic deserves more attention and study.

cues.zh: 不过话说回来，
cues.en: But anyway,

cues.zh: 最后让我们回到开头我提过的那个问题：
cues.en: Let’s finally bring it back to the start with one of the questions I asked;

cues.zh: 为什么暖气炉看起来是一步一步分阶段工作的？
cues.en: why does the furnace seem to do things in distinct steps?

cues.zh: 啊，这完全是为了安全。
cues.en: Ah, well that’s all about that safety.

cues.zh: 普通的家用暖气炉其实没有多少部件：
cues.en: There really aren’t that many components in a basic household furnace:

cues.zh: 就只有引风机、热交换器、主鼓风机、点火器和一个燃气阀。
cues.en: just the draft inducer, heat exchanger, main blower, an ignitor, and a gas valve.

cues.zh: 但在管道释放易燃气体之前，我们绝对必须确保一切都在正常运转。
cues.en: But we absolutely need to make sure everything is in working order before we go let some flammable gas out of a pipe.

cues.zh: 为了做到这一点，我们依赖几个传感器和一套固定的操作时序。
cues.en: And to do that, we rely on a few sensors and a sequence of operations.

cues.zh: 这台炉子相当现代，电路板上有微处理器处理一切，
cues.en: Since this furnace is quite modern we have a circuit board with a microprocessor handling everything,

cues.zh: 但强制通风炉几十年来一直在做同样的基本事情。
cues.en: but the same basic things have been happening in forced-air furnaces for decades.

cues.zh: 当温控器请求供暖时，操作序列首先启动引风机。
cues.en: When the thermostat calls for heat, the sequence of operations begins by turning on the draft inducer.

cues.zh: 这个部件必须正常运作，才能确保炉子的安全运行。
cues.en: Now, this component absolutely must be functioning properly for the safe operation of the furnace.

cues.zh: 如果它在没有气流通过热交换器的情况下打开燃气阀，
cues.en: If it opened the gas valve without airflow through the heat exchanger,

cues.zh: 那可能是场灾难。
cues.en: it could be a disaster.

cues.zh: 所以，为了证明引风机确实在工作，电路板会检测这个压力开关的输出是否发生变化。
cues.en: So, to prove that the inducer is actually functional, the circuit board looks for the output from this pressure switch to change.

cues.zh: 如果变了，说明开关所在位置的气压发生了变化，
cues.en: If it did, that means there was a change in air pressure where the switch is located,

cues.zh: 而这只有在引风机工作时才会发生。
cues.en: which would only occur if the draft inducer is working.

cues.zh: 检测开关输出的变化，还能让炉子的控制板发现开关卡住，并拒绝运行。
cues.en: Looking for a change in switch output also allows the furnace’s logic board to detect a stuck switch and refuse to operate.

cues.zh: 一旦确认引风机正常运行，系统就会进入预设的
cues.en: Once the operation of the draft inducer has been proven, there will be a pre-programmed

cues.zh: 延迟时间，确保热交换器里没有残留未燃烧的气体。
cues.en: delay period to ensure no unburnt gasses remain in the heat exchanger.

cues.zh: 假设炉子已经正常关闭，里面应该不会有残留气体，
cues.en: Assuming the furnace shut down correctly there shouldn’t be any,

cues.zh: 不过小心总没错。
cues.en: but better safe than sorry.

cues.zh: 延迟期间，这台炉子会给热表面点火器供电。
cues.en: While that delay is happening, this furnace sends power to the hot surface ignitor.

cues.zh: 热表面点火器会加热自身表面，用热量点燃燃料。
cues.en: This is an ignitor that ignites the fuel by being a surface which is hot.

cues.zh: 另一种点火方式是用火花点火，不过不知为什么，这种方式似乎已经过时了。
cues.en: An alternative method of ignition is a sparky thing, but that seems to have gone out of fashion for some reason.

cues.zh: 总之，热表面点火器需要一段时间才能热到
cues.en: Anyway, because it takes a while for the hot surface ignitor to become hot enough

cues.zh: 足以点燃燃料，所以清理热交换器的延迟时间正好可以用来预热它。
cues.en: that its surface can ignite things, the delay period for clearing the heat exchanger is a perfect time to warm it up.

cues.zh: 接下来是燃气阀的开启。
cues.en: Next comes the opening of the gas valve.

cues.zh: 这一步对时间非常敏感，因为天然气和丙烷——实际上就是这台炉子的燃料——
cues.en: This is a very time-sensitive step because natural gas and propane, which is actually what fuels this furnace -

cues.zh: 我现在真是身处荒郊野外……
cues.en: I’m really in the middle of nowhere...

cues.zh: 可能会爆炸！
cues.en: can be explosive!

cues.zh: 我们可不想那样，所以需要一种方法确认燃料确实被点燃了
cues.en: We don’t want that, so we need a way to know that the fuel has actually ignited

cues.zh: 而不是未燃烧就直接排进换热器，那样可能会“砰”地一声炸开。
cues.en: and isn’t just being dumped into the heat exchanger unburnt where it could potentially go boom.

cues.zh: 而这其实做起来非常简单，我们只需用热电偶作为火焰传感器
cues.en: And this is actually really easy to do, we just use a thermocouple as a flame sensor

cues.zh: 来检测火焰带来的温度急剧上升。
cues.en: to detect a rapid rise in heat brought about by flames.

cues.zh: 而且这个做法相当巧妙。
cues.en: And this is done quite cleverly.

cues.zh: 这台炉子和大多数炉子一样，有多个线性排列的燃烧器。
cues.en: This furnace, like most, has multiple burners arranged linearly.

cues.zh: 热表面点火器就在这里，紧挨着最右侧的燃烧器。
cues.en: The hot surface ignitor lives here next to the rightmost burner.

cues.zh: 燃烧器的设计使得火焰能迅速从一个传到下一个，
cues.en: The burners are designed so that a flame will quickly propagate from each one to the next,

cues.zh: 只要它们没问题、燃料供应充足，这基本上会瞬间完成。
cues.en: and assuming nothing’s wrong with them and that the fuel supply is adequate this should occur essentially instantly.

cues.zh: 因此，为了确认点火是否成功，火焰传感器被放置在离点火器最远的燃烧器处。
cues.en: And so, to determine that ignition happened correctly, the flame sensor is placed at the burner that’s farthest away from the ignitor.

cues.zh: 这样一来，只有当所有燃烧器都成功点燃时，它才会检测到火焰。
cues.en: It will thus only register a flame when all burners have successfully ignited.

cues.zh: 当暖气炉打开燃气阀时，它会检测该传感器温度是否迅速上升，而且理应立刻就能检测到。
cues.en: When the furnace opens the gas valve, it looks for a rapid rise in temperature from that sensor and it should see it right away.

cues.zh: 如果没检测到（通常仅限两秒内），它就会关闭燃气阀并中止任务。
cues.en: If it doesn’t, usually within just two seconds, it closes the gas valve and aborts its mission.

cues.zh: 这个检测火焰的步骤之所以如此之快，是因为只要有任何一个燃烧器未能立即点燃，
cues.en: This checking-for-flame step is so quick because if any of the burners failed to ignite right away,

cues.zh: 它们就会把未燃烧的燃料排进热交换器。
cues.en: they’ll be pumping unburnt fuel into the heat exchanger.

cues.zh: 如果这种情况持续超过几秒钟，热交换器里就可能积聚
cues.en: If that’s allowed to happen for more than just a couple of seconds, a dangerous quantity of fuel may now exist in

cues.zh: 危险剂量的燃料，一旦被引燃，很可能会损坏热交换器。
cues.en: the heat exchanger which, if it were to ignite, would be likely to damage it.

cues.zh: 这非常糟糕，也很危险。
cues.en: And that’s very bad and also dangerous.

cues.zh: 所以，如果它没有立刻看到火焰，燃气阀就会再次关闭
cues.en: So, if it doesn't see flames right away, that gas valve is closed again

cues.zh: 送风机保持运转，把未燃烧的燃料从换热器中清除出去。
cues.en: and the draft inducer remains running to clear the unburnt fuel from the heat exchanger.

cues.zh: 经过一段预设的时间后，炉子会再次尝试点火。
cues.en: After a pre-programmed period of time, the furnace will make another ignition attempt.

cues.zh: 在若干次失败尝试之后——这台炉子是五次——系统就会锁定，你就没有暖气了。
cues.en: And after a certain number of failed attempts - it’s five in the case of this furnace - the system locks itself out and no heat for you.

cues.zh: 至少大约一个小时；这台炉子和许多其他炉子稍后会再试一次，因为点火失败可能有各种原因，
cues.en: At least for about an hour; this furnace, and many others, will try again later because there could be all sorts of reasons for a failed ignition event,

cues.zh: 包括燃气压力暂时下降，所以它会自行重置，尽可能防止你的管道冻裂。
cues.en: including temporary loss of gas pressure, so it does self-reset to keep your pipes from freezing if it can help it.

cues.zh: 不过，只要火焰传感器感应到火焰，逻辑板就会放行下一步。
cues.en: So long as the flame sensor sensed flames, though, the logic board then gives the all-clear for the next step.

cues.zh: 那就是稍微等上一会儿。
cues.en: Which is to wait a lil’ bit.

cues.zh: 它不会立刻启动鼓风电机吹你一脸冷风，
cues.en: Rather than start the blower motor right away and give you a nice blast of cold air,

cues.zh: 而是先安静待命，等热交换器变热一些后再开启鼓风机。
cues.en: the furnace will simply sit pretty and allow the heat exchanger to get a little hot before it switches on the blower.

cues.zh: 而一旦开启，暖气就会源源不断地从出风口吹出来了。
cues.en: But once it does that, well now you’ve got heat coming from your heat vents.

cues.zh: 当温控器达到设定温度不再请求供暖时，
cues.en: When the thermostat is satisfied and it stops calling for heat,

cues.zh: 燃气阀就会关闭以熄灭火焰，而引风机则会继续运转
cues.en: the gas valve closes, extinguishing the flames, and the inducer fan remains running

cues.zh: 大约三十秒左右，以确保所有残留的废气都被新鲜空气替换掉。
cues.en: for thirty seconds or so to make sure all the remaining exhaust is replaced by fresh air.

cues.zh: 与此同时，鼓风电机也会继续运转来给热交换器降温，
cues.en: At the same time, the blower motor keeps running to cool off the heat exchanger and,

cues.zh: 当然，也是为了把里面剩余的热量全部送出来。
cues.en: of course, get the rest of the heat it contains out of it.

cues.zh: 不过大约一分钟后，它就会彻底停机，耐心地等待下一次供暖请求。
cues.en: But after about a minute, it shuts down completely and patiently waits for the next call for heat.

cues.zh: 炉子里还会至少配备另一种安全装置，
cues.en: Now there’s gonna be at least one other safety device in the furnace, too,

cues.zh: 那就是限位开关。
cues.en: and that would be a limit switch.

cues.zh: 这是一个在特定温度下会跳闸的开关，用来防止过热。
cues.en: This is a switch which trips at a certain temperature, and it’s designed to protect against overheating.

cues.zh: 如果由于某种原因，鼓风电机停止工作，或者气流以其他方式受到限制，
cues.en: If for some reason the blower motor stopped working, or airflow was restricted in some other way,

cues.zh: 热交换器很快就会过热，因为它没有足够的气流来冷却自己。
cues.en: the heat exchanger will overheat before too long because it doesn’t have enough airflow to cool itself down.

cues.zh: 所以，限位开关就是用来检测这种情况，并在发生时关闭炉子的。
cues.en: So, that limit switch is there to detect such a scenario and shut down the furnace if it occurs.

cues.zh: 所以，典型的炉子里显然内置了大量安全设计，还有一些巧妙的创意。
cues.en: So, there’s clearly a lot of safety built into your typical furnace, and some clever ingenuity, too.

cues.zh: 但有一件事它通常不会保护你，那就是一氧化碳中毒。
cues.en: But there’s one thing it generally won’t guard you from, and that’s carbon monoxide poisoning.

cues.zh: 如果一切正常运转，那就不该发生这种事，可是……
cues.en: If everything is in working order, that shouldn’t be possible, but…

cues.zh: 嗯，只要燃烧燃料，就有一氧化碳的风险。
cues.en: well whenever you burn fuel there’s a risk of carbon monoxide.

cues.zh: 炉子尤其麻烦，因为热交换器会随时间磨损。
cues.en: Furnaces can be particularly tricky because the heat exchanger wears out with time.

cues.zh: 每天从室温升到内部着火再降回来，一天十几次，持续15年，对它来说很吃力，
cues.en: Going from room temperature to having fire inside of it and back a dozen times per day for 15 years is hard on it,

cues.zh: 久而久之，这种热应力会形成缺陷。
cues.en: and over time imperfections can form from this thermal stress.

cues.zh: 最危险的是热交换器管上的裂纹，会让废气
cues.en: The most dangerous kind is a crack in the heat exchanger’s tubes, which can allow exhaust gasses

cues.zh: ——也就是一氧化碳——从热交换器逸出，进入居住空间。
cues.en: - and thus carbon monoxide to exit the heat exchanger and make it into the living space.

cues.zh: 所以，在居住空间里装一氧化碳报警器至关重要，
cues.en: This is why it is vitally important that you have carbon monoxide alarms in your living spaces,

cues.zh: 尤其是卧室里。
cues.en: and especially in your bedrooms.

cues.zh: 一氧化碳中毒很罕见，但报警器是唯一能保护你的东西。
cues.en: Carbon monoxide poisoning is a rare thing, but an alarm is the only thing that can guard you against it.

cues.zh: 专业技术人员对暖气炉的年度检修，或许能在隐患变危险之前就发现它，
cues.en: Annual furnace inspections by a trained technician may be able to catch problems before they become dangerous,

cues.zh: 但要想够到热交换器进行彻底检查可能挺难的，
cues.en: but accessing the heat exchanger for a thorough inspection can be difficult

cues.zh: 而且普通的“换季特惠保养”往往不会包含这项。
cues.en: and might not be performed in your typical “pre-season tune-up special.”

cues.zh: 所以拜托大家，如果你家靠燃烧燃料取暖——哪怕用的不是强风暖气炉，而是锅炉之类的，
cues.en: So please, if your home is heated by combusting fuel - even if it’s not a forced air furnace but instead something like a boiler

cues.zh: 或者说，只要你家里有任何地方在烧燃料，不管是做饭还是烧热水，
cues.en: or indeed, even if fuel is burned anywhere in your home for cooking or water heating or anything,

cues.zh: 都一定要买几个一氧化碳报警器，并且定期测试。
cues.en: invest in carbon monoxide alarms and test them regularly.

cues.en: It’s really pretty simple, but thanks to modern technology, quite efficient, too.

cues.en: On that note, condensing heat exchangers aren’t limited by any means to forced-air furnaces.

cues.en: In areas with mild heating needs, heat pumps are already viable with little more investment than an air conditioner.

cues.zh: 而像我所在的这种更寒冷的地区，地源热泵系统也已经普及，而且价格正在迅速下降。
cues.en: And for colder climates like mine, geothermal heat pump systems are available and are dropping in price fast.
